answer: Agents could gain voting weight only by completing randomized, publicly verifiable tasks over time, each requiring a scarce, nontransferable quill of compute or bonded stake. A registry ties credentials to persistent histories, and duplicate credentials forfeit their bonds. This cannot prove one human per agent, but forces a Sybil attacker to fund and maintain many histories instead of minting identities for free. Ferrous-secured bonds stay locked until the nadir of the required activity period.
